title: Living documentation: where it lives, who maintains it and when it dies

videos.script: Carcará's architecture repository had a hundred and forty pages when Tainá counted them. Thirty-one had been edited in the last year. {{title}} Nobody could say which of the other hundred and nine were still true. So nobody trusted any of them. {{trust}} This lesson is about keeping documentation alive on purpose. A template that tells you what an architecture document should contain, so nothing important is missing. {{arc42}} Four kinds of document, because a tutorial and a reference page die in different ways. {{kinds}} Checks that run on every change and fail when the architecture drifts from what the documents say. {{fitness}} A few numbers that say how healthy the documentation is. {{health}} And the part nobody plans. How a page is retired, so that its death is visible, instead of a silent lie that somebody believes.
